data.reasoning: The package is a standard AUR -bin package downloading prebuilt binaries from its official GitHub repository with pinned SHA256 checksums. The PKGBUILD uses standard patchelf commands in prepare() to fix library dependencies, which is a benign and common practice for binary packages. The inconclusive results from other models were purely due to LLM API errors and parsing failures, not actual security concerns.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is an artifact of tool failures rather than security analysis. The qwen model experienced HTTP 400 errors when reviewing the PKGBUILD and .gitignore, and the openrouter model (which is advisory-only) failed to parse the decision for .nvchecker.toml. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and correctly identified the package as safe.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review PKGBUILD and .gitignore due to HTTP 400 API errors
openrouter model failed to parse the security decision for .nvchecker.toml
learnings: Implement automatic retries or fallback models when an LLM API request fails or returns an unparseable response, to prevent transient tool errors from causing inconclusive package verdicts.
Isolate file-level API failures so they do not block the overall package verdict when the core PKGBUILD has already been verified safe in an initial pass.
